newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish insurance watchdog urges PZU to up equity.
newsitem.headline: Polish insurance watchdog urges PZU to up equity.

text.p: Poland's insurance supervision chief urged on Wednesday the country's largest insurer, state-owned Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen SA (PZU) to boost capital quickly to meet solvency requirements.
Danuta Walcerz, the head of the State Insurance Supervision Office, told reporters: "The PZU lacks about 400 million zlotys to cover the solvency margin.
"I cannot tolerate the situation in PZU. I have assured the finance minister that I would place the company under direct administration if it fails to raise its capital to required levels."
PZU president Jan Monkiewicz confirmed earlier plans to raise between 250 million and 800 million zlotys through private placement to meet the safety requirements.
Monkiewicz said the finance minister representing the state treasury would decide on November 29 on the new share issue for the first quarter of 1997.
"Capital needs are estimated at between 250 and 800 million zlotys and the issue's size would fall within this range," he said.

Earlier this month, PZU announced it would seek to raise $200-300 million through a private placement to a group of selected institutional investors, possibly also including the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).

The company is also mulling a public offering, which could take place no sooner than the fourth quarter of 1996, but PZU has no specific plans, Monkiewicz said. He said the shortage of capital was largely a result of a fast growth of premium revenues.

PZU, which in the first three quarters of this year collected a total of 2.7 billion zlotys in gross premiums, has a 61 percent share of Poland's non-life market and, together with PZU Zycie, about 70 percent of the total insurance business.
